title: Selected-time weak adjoint equation for common-reference densities
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling: Proposition 1.2.6 gives the forward law equation in adjoint form, and Theorem 8.3.1 uses the time-dependent identities partial_t mu_t = L_t^* mu_t and partial_t nu_t = L_t^* nu_t by testing them against frozen observables. In a fixed common-reference density presentation this is the selected-time pairing integral phi * densityDot dxi = integral (L_t phi) * density dxi.
target_statement: Introduce a reusable selected-time weak-density contract on an explicit test domain: for every admissible phi, both phi*densityDot and (L phi)*density are integrable against the common reference measure and their integrals agree. Do not claim that densityDot is the time derivative of a path, construct an adjoint operator, or specialize to a fixed semigroup.

shared_floor_audit.notes: This adapts the semantic content of Samplinglib's fixed-semigroup WeakForwardEquation to the selected-time density form actually consumed by Chewi 8.3.1. It deliberately records both pairing integrabilities: equality of totalized Bochner integrals alone is not evidence that either integrand is analytically admissible. The contract is selected-time so an arbitrary time-dependent generator family can supply one instance at each time without pretending it is a homogeneous semigroup. The exact theorem head compiled in both focused targets and then passed the full ASTIS root gate without statement repair.
